description: The article proposes a pragmatic distinction between complexity and difficulty measures for well-structured problems in learning systems: \"a complexity measure is based only on the item description, it does not use any data about student performance; a difficulty measure is based only on data about
title: Pragmatic complexity–difficulty distinction for well-structured learning items

description: The report's key conclusions state that the Hampshire Hundreds project \"illustrates the importance of careful piloting of an intervention before attempting an impact evaluation\".
title: Pre-impact piloting of intervention delivery and measurement procedures

description: The article recommends that evaluators discuss \"appropriate precision standards\" and then determine, for each random-assignment design, \"the required number of schools to achieve those standards\" using empirical parameter values.
title: Precision-based sample-size planning for clustered education trials

description: The precursor question relation is the article's formal account of empirical relationships between test items: question A is a precursor of B when f(A,B)=P(B=1|A=0)/P(B=1|A=1) falls below a threshold, an \"adaptation of the relative risk index to the context of a multiple-choice test\" with Cohen's d
title: Precursor question relation

description: The article articulates a framework distinguishing explanatory from predictive statistical modelling.
title: Prediction versus explanation as two cultures of statistical modelling in educational psychology

description: A data augmentation technique in which, instead of sliding windows or cropping, \"we generate all prefixes of each sequence (from length 1 to n), allowing the model to learn to make predictions at any point in a student's progression\".
title: Prefix-based data augmentation for early prediction in educational sequences

description: PLAF is a step-by-step framework with two key components, predictive and prescriptive phases, for identifying at-risk learners and generating evidence-based remedial advice.
title: Prescriptive Learning Analytics Framework (PLAF)

description: The article develops a framework that models students as a mixture of latent subgroups, each defined by the pair of care types a child would receive with and without a Head Start offer (e.g., \"Center Compliers\" and \"Always Head Start\").
title: Principal stratification with hierarchical random effects and Bayesian estimation

description: PTA is a data-driven methodology that \"produces a representative set of textual descriptions we callprincipal traitsfrom a corpus of human collaborator-AI collaborative conversation sessions.\" It runs four stages: LLM-prompted behavior-observation extraction (generic or theory-lens), embedding-based
title: Principal Trait Analysis (PTA)

description: The framework translates pedagogical design principles into observable indicators using a compact mapping (Table I) from principle to indicator to observation method: transparency of identity and limits (misinterpretation rate via survey/observation), scaffolding toward humans (transition-to-human p
title: Principle-to-indicator mapping as an accountability device for AI-enabled pedagogical systems

description: PRISMA-LLM is an evidence-informed reporting framework for LLM-assisted and AI-enabled systematic-review workflows, organized to complement PRISMA 2020.
title: PRISMA-LLM: a three-layer reporting framework for LLM-assisted systematic reviews

description: A four-stage framework in which heterogeneous commercial LLMs (LLaMA-3.3-70B, GPT-4o-mini, Claude-3-Haiku) independently predict student knowledge states via engineered prompts, add calibrated Laplace noise locally to their prediction outputs, and aggregate with residual correction.
title: Privacy-preserving heterogeneous multi-LLM federated inference framework for cognitive diagnosis

description: The article presents a worked scenario in which a DLP used across several school districts for high school math instruction is linked with state college enrollment and persistence records using secure multiparty computation, producing aggregate correlations between engagement patterns and college ou
title: Privacy-preserving linkage and analysis of educational data using privacy-enhancing technologies

description: The article introduces a family of Bayesian models in which each submission has a latent true score, each grader a bias (tendency to \"inﬂate or deﬂate her assessment\") and a reliability (precision of assessments after bias correction).
title: Probabilistic peer grading models (PG1, PG2, PG3)

description: A scoring account in which each stimulus word's difficulty is estimated from the percentage of subjects failing it, then converted to a percentile value by reading from a table based on the area of the probability curve, assuming the tested ability fits that curve.
title: Probability-curve percentile weighting of item difficulty for scoring opposites tests

description: The paper argues SEERNet's contribution \"could be enhanced by integrating a problem-based approach inspired by Improvement Science—that is, by collaborating with educators to identify the right problem of practice to focus on\".
title: Problem-of-practice-driven research-practice partnership

description: The study employs an adapted version of the Process Mining Methodology (PM2) with seven steps, from definition of objectives to evaluation of process models, using the Disco Fluxicon software tool with an adapted Fuzzy Minner algorithm.
title: Process mining methodology for MOOC event logs (adapted PM2)

description: When both restudy and test condition means shift in the same direction across levels of another factor, an ANOVA interaction on proportion correct is theoretically uninterpretable, because the mapping from latent memory strength to accuracy is non-linear and unknown.
title: Process-model and distribution-matching method for testing moderation of testing efficacy

description: PSW methods operationalize a cognitive discrepancy approach to LD identification based on identifying an intraindividual pattern of processing strengths and weaknesses.
title: Processing strengths and weaknesses (PSW) approaches to learning-disability identification

description: The study's method is a projection framework rather than a direct measurement of pandemic learning loss.
title: Projection approach combining absenteeism-literature estimates with summer learning pattern analyses

description: Promotion power is a measure of school effectiveness that the study defines as distinguishing \"a school's contributions to student outcomes from the contributions of the background characteristics of the students it serves.\" It accounts for prior achievement and other background characteristics, and
title: Promotion power measure of school effectiveness

description: The article describes a framework of prompting techniques — Vanilla, Chain of Thought, and Self-Ask — applied with zero-shot and few-shot strategies to detect teacher questions from ASR outputs.
title: Prompt engineering techniques for LLM-based classroom discourse analysis

description: When estimating the achievement effects of school transfer or school choice from non-experimental data, the article recommends combining propensity score stratification with multilevel models.
title: Propensity score stratification with multilevel models

description: A multistep design-based method for selecting experiment sites so the sample resembles a defined inference population.
title: Propensity-score stratified site-selection method for improving generalization from experiments

description: ProPRL is a framework that learns prerequisite relations over ordered concept pairs in educational knowledge graphs.
title: ProPRL: property-aware framework for prerequisite relation learning

description: The article recommends that evaluators apply the value-conflict taxonomy prospectively rather than only retrospectively.
title: Prospective value-conflict analysis for educational evaluation
